trigger_condition.shape_trigger: out= tensor shape may differ from the inferred torch.cat output shape
trigger_condition.device_trigger: CPU and CUDA backends are both used for comparison
trigger_condition.memory_trigger: Input tensors have mixed memory formats, such as contiguous and channels_last
trigger_condition.execution_trigger: torch.cat is called with the out= variant
trigger_condition.concrete_constraints: Use torch.cat([A, B], dim=d, out=output) with multiple input tensors, where at least one input uses channels_last and another uses contiguous memory format; run on CPU and CUDA and inspect output memory_format.

root_cause.aten_layer: torch.cat out= CPU and CUDA variants use different strategies to determine output memory format
root_cause.backend_layer: CPU inherits memory format from the first input tensor, while CUDA recomputes memory format using compute_output_memory_format over all inputs

bug_oracle.description: The same torch.cat out= operation produces different output memory_format behavior on CPU and CUDA when inputs have mixed memory formats.
bug_oracle.signal: output.memory_format differs between CPU and CUDA

harness_strategy.input_mutation: Vary input tensor memory formats among contiguous, channels_last, and other supported layouts
harness_strategy.tensor_construction: Construct multiple input tensors with explicitly different memory formats and allocate an out= tensor whose shape may not match the inferred cat output shape
harness_strategy.constraint_injection: Ensure at least one input tensor is non-contiguous or channels_last while another is contiguous, and execute the same operation on CPU and CUDA
harness_strategy.operation_sequence: Create mixed-memory-format input tensors, call torch.cat(..., out=output), then inspect the output tensor memory_format
harness_strategy.oracle_construction: Assert that CPU and CUDA outputs have equivalent memory_format, or compare against a documented memory format selection rule
